text:
raj.patel: Hi, after our IdP rotated certs this morning some users can't SSO into prod. Getting 403 with 'RecipientMismatch' in our SP logs. Started ~06:45 UTC.
maya.support: Sorry — can you paste the SAMLResponse error or the SP log snippet? Any ACS URL changes on your side?
raj.patel: SP log (masked): Accepting SAMLResponse but error: RecipientMismatch. ACS=https://app.example.com/saml/acs but Assertion Recipient=https://login.example.com/saml/acs
maya.support: That looks like an ACS mismatch. Did the IdP change metadata or add a proxy ACS? Any CDN/edge rewrite in front of the IdP?
carl.oncall: Oncall checking metadata poll history. We fetched new idp.xml at 06:44:58 (sha256:aa12f9...).
carl.oncall: Validation flagged "certificate chain incomplete" on that fetch but signature verified.
jenna.iam: IdP said they rotated signing and encryption certs and also pushed a metadata update that added an alternate ACS and a different entityID alias.
raj.patel: They insist they only rotated certs. But some users work and others hit 403.
maya.support: Two likely causes: 1) IdP added an alternate ACS and put it first in the AssertionConsumerService list so our parser selects the wrong Recipient; 2) cert chain problems cause our automated metadata upload to be skipped and we kept old metadata.
maya.support: Can you share their metadata endpoint?
raj.patel: https://idp.example.net/metadata.xml
maya.support: Quick check (example):
```
curl -s https://idp.example.net/metadata.xml | xmllint --format - | sed -n '1,160p'
```
maya.support: I see two AssertionConsumerService entries. First: Location="https://login.example.com/saml/acs" index="0"; Second: Location="https://app.example.com/saml/acs" index="1"
carl.oncall: Our SP is configured for https://app.example.com/saml/acs. Because IdP placed the proxy/login ACS first, assertions use that Recipient and ours rejects them.
jenna.iam: Remediations: (A) Ask IdP to remove/reorder alt-acs so canonical app ACS is first; (B) manually upload corrected metadata into our Console; (C) short-term enable accept-assertion-recipient-aliases flag (requires controlled deploy).
raj.patel: We tried manual upload but got "certificate chain incomplete". How to proceed?
maya.support: That error means the metadata's X.509 cert is missing intermediate cert(s). Two options: 1) Ask IdP to publish full PEM chain in metadata; 2) download their certs and upload the full concatenated chain when you upload metadata.
jenna.iam: Example concat file format to upload: 
```
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF... (idp signing)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIC... (intermediate)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```
maya.support: Steps for manual patch: 1) curl -o idp.xml https://idp.example.net/metadata.xml; 2) edit AssertionConsumerService entries so Location="https://app.example.com/saml/acs" has index="0"; update index attributes; 3) Console -> SSO -> IdP config -> Upload metadata; 4) Admin -> Force metadata reload; 5) test SSO in incognito.
carl.oncall: If upload still rejects, paste combined cert PEM into the upload UI or use the API to set raw metadata with chain.
raj.patel: Upload with full chain succeeded. Some users regained access, a few still 403.
carl.oncall: Remaining failures are coming from mobile clients hitting the proxy domain (login.example.com) which still receives assertions with Recipient set to login.example.com. We'll add a redirect/mapping on the proxy so Recipient matches https://app.example.com/saml/acs for those requests.
maya.support: sso-bot shows: metadata-poller fetched idp.example.net/metadata.xml at 06:46:12, signature ok, chain incomplete -> manual upload required.
sso-bot: metadata-poller: status -> manual action taken at 06:49:22, metadata replaced by admin upload.
raj.patel: After the proxy mapping + metadata upload, tests look good. A couple of edge cases on older mobile SDKs still failing, likely cached metadata or hardcoded ACS. We're chasing them.
maya.support: I'll keep the thread open for 30m to confirm stability. If you see any new 403s, paste the SP debug line.
raj.patel: Thanks all :tada:
maya.support: :thumbsup:
